p.src: Sons of Mieding, rest to-day! Needless your machinery: Misty vale and mountain gray, That is all the scenery.

u.src: Needless your machinery: Misty vale and mountain gray, That is all the scenery.

p.src: That the wedding golden be, Must fifty years be rounded: But the Golden give to me, When the strife’s compounded.

u.src: That the wedding golden be, Must fifty years be rounded: But the Golden give to me, When the strife’s compounded.

p.src: Spirits, if you’re here, be seen— Show yourselves, delighted! Fairy king and fairy queen, They are newly plighted.

u.src: Spirits, if you’re here, be seen— Show yourselves, delighted!
Fairy king and fairy queen, They are newly plighted.

p.src: Cometh Puck, and, light of limb, Whisks and whirls in measure: Come a hundred after him, To share with him the pleasure.

u.src: Cometh Puck, and, light of limb, Whisks and whirls in measure: Come a hundred after him, To share with him the pleasure.

p.src: Ariel’s song is heavenly-pure, His tones are sweet and rare ones: Though ugly faces he allure, Yet he allures the fair ones.

u.src: Ariel’s song is heavenly-pure, His tones are sweet and rare ones: Though ugly faces he allure, Yet he allures the fair ones.

p.src: Spouses, who would fain agree, Learn how we were mated! If your pairs would loving be, First be separated!

u.src: Spouses, who would fain agree, Learn how we were mated!
If your pairs would loving be, First be separated!

p.src: If her whims the wife control, And the man berate her, Take him to the Northern Pole, And her to the Equator!

u.src: If her whims the wife control, And the man berate her, Take him to the Northern Pole, And her to the Equator!

p.src: Snout of fly, mosquito-bill, And kin of all conditions, Frog in grass, and cricket-trill,— These are the musicians!

u.src: Snout of fly, mosquito-bill, And kin of all conditions, Frog in grass, and cricket-trill,— These are the musicians!

p.src: See the bagpipe on our track! ’Tis the soap-blown bubble: Hear the schnecke-schnicke-schnack Through his nostrils double!

u.src: See the bagpipe on our track!

u.src: ’Tis the soap-blown bubble: Hear the schnecke-schnicke-schnack Through his nostrils double!

p.src: Spider’s foot and paunch of toad, And little wings—we know ’em! A little creature ’twill not be, But yet, a little poem.

u.src: Spider’s foot and paunch of toad, And little wings—we know ’em!
A little creature ’twill not be, But yet, a little poem.

p.src: Little step and lofty leap Through honey-dew and fragrance: You’ll never mount the airy steep With all your tripping vagrance.

u.src: Little step and lofty leap Through honey-dew and fragrance: You’ll never mount the airy steep With all your tripping vagrance.

p.src: Is’t but masquerading play? See I with precision? Oberon, the beauteous fay, Meets, to-night, my vision!

u.src: Oberon, the beauteous fay, Meets, to-night, my vision!

p.src: Not a claw, no tail I see! And yet, beyond a cavil, Like “the Gods of Greece,” must he Also be a devil.

u.src: Not a claw, no tail I see!
And yet, beyond a cavil, Like “the Gods of Greece,” must he Also be a devil.

p.src: I only seize, with sketchy air, Some outlines of the tourney; Yet I betimes myself prepare For my Italian journey.

u.src: I only seize, with sketchy air, Some outlines of the tourney; Yet I betimes myself prepare For my Italian journey.

p.src: My bad luck brings me here, alas! How roars the orgy louder! And of the witches in the mass, But only two wear powder.

u.src: My bad luck brings me here, alas!
And of the witches in the mass, But only two wear powder.

p.src: Powder becomes, like petticoat, A gray and wrinkled noddy; So I sit naked on my goat, And show a strapping body.

u.src: Powder becomes, like petticoat, A gray and wrinkled noddy; So I sit naked on my goat, And show a strapping body.

p.src: We’ve too much tact and policy To rate with gibes a scolder; Yet, young and tender though you be, I hope to see you moulder.

u.src: We’ve too much tact and policy To rate with gibes a scolder; Yet, young and tender though you be, I hope to see you moulder.

p.src: Fly-snout and mosquito-bill, Don’t swarm so round the Naked! Frog in grass and cricket-trill, Observe the time, and make it!

u.src: Fly-snout and mosquito-bill, Don’t swarm so round the Naked!
Frog in grass and cricket-trill, Observe the time, and make it!

p.src: Society to one’s desire! Brides only, and the sweetest! And bachelors of youth and fire. And prospects the completest!

u.src: And bachelors of youth and fire.

p.src: And if the Earth don’t open now To swallow up each ranter, Why, then will I myself, I vow, Jump into hell instanter!

u.src: And if the Earth don’t open now To swallow up each ranter, Why, then will I myself, I vow, Jump into hell instanter!

p.src: Us as little insects see! With sharpest nippers flitting, That our Papa Satan we May honor as is fitting.

u.src: With sharpest nippers flitting, That our Papa Satan we May honor as is fitting.

p.src: How, in crowds together massed, They are jesting, shameless! They will even say, at last, That their hearts are blameless.

u.src: How, in crowds together massed, They are jesting, shameless!
They will even say, at last, That their hearts are blameless.

p.src: Among this witches’ revelry His way one gladly loses; And, truly, it would easier be Than to command the Muses.

u.src: Among this witches’ revelry His way one gladly loses; And, truly, it would easier be Than to command the Muses.

p.src: The proper folks one’s talents laud: Come on, and none shall pass us! The Blocksberg has a summit broad, Like Germany’s Parnassus.

u.src: The proper folks one’s talents laud: Come on, and none shall pass us!
The Blocksberg has a summit broad, Like Germany’s Parnassus.

p.src: Say, who’s the stiff and pompous man? He walks with haughty paces: He snuffles all he snuffle can: “He scents the Jesuits’ traces.”

u.src: Say, who’s the stiff and pompous man?
He walks with haughty paces: He snuffles all he snuffle can: “He scents the Jesuits’ traces.”

p.src: Both clear and muddy streams, for me Are good to fish and sport in: And thus the pious man you see With even devils consorting.

u.src: Both clear and muddy streams, for me Are good to fish and sport in: And thus the pious man you see With even devils consorting.

p.src: Yes, for the pious, I suspect, All instruments are fitting; And on the Blocksberg they erect Full many a place of meeting.

u.src: Yes, for the pious, I suspect, All instruments are fitting; And on the Blocksberg they erect Full many a place of meeting.

p.src: A newer chorus now succeeds! I hear the distant drumming. “Don’t be disturbed! ’tis, in the reeds, The bittern’s changeless booming.”

u.src: ’tis, in the reeds, The bittern’s changeless booming.”

p.src: How each his legs in nimble trip Lifts up, and makes a clearance! The crooked jump, the heavy skip, Nor care for the appearance.

u.src: How each his legs in nimble trip Lifts up, and makes a clearance!
The crooked jump, the heavy skip, Nor care for the appearance.

p.src: The rabble by such hate are held, To maim and slay delights them: As Orpheus’ lyre the brutes compelled, The bagpipe here unites them.

u.src: The rabble by such hate are held, To maim and slay delights them: As Orpheus’ lyre the brutes compelled, The bagpipe here unites them.

p.src: I’ll not be led by any lure Of doubts or critic-cavils: The Devil must be something, sure,— Or how should there be devils?

u.src: I’ll not be led by any lure Of doubts or critic-cavils: The Devil must be something, sure,— Or how should there be devils?

p.src: This once, the fancy wrought in me Is really too despotic: Forsooth, if I am all I see, I must be idiotic!

u.src: This once, the fancy wrought in me Is really too despotic: Forsooth, if I am all I see, I must be idiotic!

p.src: This racking fuss on every hand, It gives me great vexation; And, for the first time, here I stand On insecure foundation.

u.src: This racking fuss on every hand, It gives me great vexation; And, for the first time, here I stand On insecure foundation.

p.src: With much delight I see the play, And grant to these their merits, Since from the devils I also may Infer the better spirits.

u.src: With much delight I see the play, And grant to these their merits, Since from the devils I also may Infer the better spirits.

p.src: The flame they follow, on and on, And think they’re near the treasure: But Devil rhymes with Doubt alone, So I am here with pleasure.

u.src: The flame they follow, on and on, And think they’re near the treasure: But Devil rhymes with Doubt alone, So I am here with pleasure.

p.src: Frog in green, and cricket-trill. Such dilettants!—perdition! Fly-snout and mosquito-bill,— Each one’s a fine musician!

u.src: Fly-snout and mosquito-bill,— Each one’s a fine musician!

p.src: Sans souci, we call the clan Of merry creatures so, then; Go a-foot no more we can, And on our heads we go, then.

u.src: Sans souci, we call the clan Of merry creatures so, then; Go a-foot no more we can, And on our heads we go, then.

p.src: Once many a bit we sponged, but now, God help us! that is done with: Our shoes are all danced out, we trow, We’ve but naked soles to run with.

u.src: Once many a bit we sponged, but now, God help us! that is done with: Our shoes are all danced out, we trow, We’ve but naked soles to run with.

p.src: From the marshes we appear, Where we originated; Yet in the ranks, at once, we’re here As glittering gallants rated.

u.src: From the marshes we appear, Where we originated; Yet in the ranks, at once, we’re here As glittering gallants rated.

p.src: Darting hither from the sky, In star and fire light shooting, Cross-wise now in grass I lie: Who’ll help me to my footing?

u.src: Darting hither from the sky, In star and fire light shooting, Cross-wise now in grass I lie: Who’ll help me to my footing?

p.src: Room! and round about us, room! Trodden are the grasses: Spirits also, spirits come, And they are bulky masses.

u.src: Room! and round about us, room!
Trodden are the grasses: Spirits also, spirits come, And they are bulky masses.

p.src: Enter not so stall-fed quite, Like elephant-calves about one! And the heaviest weight to-night Be Puck, himself, the stout one!

u.src: Enter not so stall-fed quite, Like elephant-calves about one!
And the heaviest weight to-night Be Puck, himself, the stout one!

p.src: If loving Nature at your back, Or Mind, the wings uncloses, Follow up my airy track To the mount of roses!

u.src: If loving Nature at your back, Or Mind, the wings uncloses, Follow up my airy track To the mount of roses!

p.src: pianissimo Cloud and trailing mist o’erhead Are now illuminated: Air in leaves, and wind in reed, And all is dissipated.

u.src: pianissimo Cloud and trailing mist o’erhead Are now illuminated: Air in leaves, and wind in reed, And all is dissipated.
